questions.question: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is a Roman Catholic basilica located in the state of ___________ and is a UNESCO world Heritage Site.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Basilica of Bom Jesus is located in Old Goa, which was the capital of Portuguese India.
 
• It is one of the oldest churches in Goa and is a significant example of Baroque architecture in India.
 
• The basilica holds the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, a prominent Catholic missionary.
 
• In 1986, the Basilica of Bom Jesus was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its historical and architectural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baroque Architecture**

 
 
• Baroque architecture is characterized by dramatic use of light, bold decorations, and grandeur.
 
• It originated in Italy in the early 17th century and spread across Europe and the Americas.
 
 
 
• **St. Francis Xavier**
 
 
• St. Francis Xavier was a Spanish Roman Catholic missionary and co-founder of the Society of Jesus (Jesuits).
 
• He is known for his extensive missionary work in Asia, especially in India and Japan.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**
 
 
• UNESCO designates places of cultural or natural importance as World Heritage Sites to encourage their preservation.
 
• As of 2023, India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including monuments, natural parks, and historical buildings.
 
 
 
• **Portuguese India**
 
 
• Portuguese India refers to the territories in India that were under Portuguese colonial rule from 1505 to 1961.
 
• Goa was the most prominent part of Portuguese India and served as the capital of Portuguese colonial possessions in Asia.

questions.question:
A cut twig is placed in coloured water as shown in the diagram below. After a few hours, when the twig is cut, how will it look (where will we find the coloured tissue)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ba85e8db1dc9a9e24ad61ca3311dddf3eceafb8a8296b3982b945b9f0eebdbf.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Like figure A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a cut twig is placed in colored water, the colored water is absorbed through the xylem vessels.
 
• Xylem vessels are responsible for the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to different parts of the plant.
 
• The colored water travels up the stem and reaches the leaves, coloring the xylem tissue along the way.
 
• The colored tissue will be visible in the xylem of the stem when the twig is cut after a few hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem Tissue**

 
 
• Xylem is one of the two types of transport tissue in vascular plants, the other being phloem.
 
• Xylem primarily conducts water and dissolved minerals from the roots to various parts of the plant.
 
• It also provides mechanical support to the plant.
 
• Xylem is composed of specialized cells like tracheids and vessel elements.
 
 
 
• **Capillary Action**
 
 
• Capillary action is the ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of external forces like gravity.
 
• It plays a key role in the movement of water (and colored solution) through the xylem in plants.
 
• This phenomenon is due to the adhesive and cohesive forces of water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**
 
 
• Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, mainly from the leaves.
 
• It creates a negative pressure that pulls water up through the xylem vessels from the roots.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Plants**
 
 
• Vascular plants are plants that have specialized tissues (xylem and phloem) for conducting water, minerals, and photosynthetic products throughout the plant.
 
• Examples include ferns, conifers, and flowering plants.

questions.question: During a sale, a trader allows a 25% cash discount followed by a 10% trade discount. If the list price of an item is Rs. 800, then its selling price is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

List price of an item = Rs. 800

Cash discount allowed = 25%

Trade discount allowed = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling price after cash discount = List price x (1 - Cash discount)

Selling price after trade discount = Selling price after cash discount x (1 - Trade discount)

**Calculation:**

Selling price after cash discount:

⇒ 800 x (1 - 0.25)

⇒ 800 x 0.75 = 600

Selling price after trade discount:

⇒ 600 x (1 - 0.10)

⇒ 600 x 0.90 = 540

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 540.**

questions.question: Which of the following is used for removing permanent hardness of water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na2CO3 10H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Na2CO3 10H2O** (Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate), also known as washing soda, is used to remove permanent hardness of water.
 
• Permanent hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium and magnesium salts, particularly in the form of chlorides and sulfates.
 
• Washing soda works by precipitating out calcium and magnesium ions as their respective carbonates, thus softening the water.
 
• This method is efficient and widely used in both domestic and industrial water softening processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temporary Hardness**

 
 
• Temporary hardness is primarily caused by the presence of dissolved bicarbonate minerals (calcium bicarbonate and magnesium bicarbonate).
 
• It can be removed by boiling the water, which decomposes the bicarbonates into carbonates, water, and carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Hardness**
 
 
• Permanent hardness is caused by sulfate and chloride compounds of calcium and magnesium.
 
• It cannot be removed by boiling and requires chemical treatment for removal.
 
 
 
• **Ion Exchange Method**
 
 
• Another method to remove permanent hardness is using ion exchange resins which replace calcium and magnesium ions with sodium or potassium ions.
 
• This method is commonly used in water softeners.
 
 
 
• **Zeolite Process**
 
 
• In this method, hard water is passed through a bed of zeolite (hydrated sodium aluminosilicate) which exchanges its sodium ions for calcium and magnesium ions, thus softening the water.
 
• The exhausted zeolite can be regenerated by washing it with a concentrated solution of sodium chloride.

questions.question: Two sides of a triangular field are 41 m and 28 m. If its perimeter is 84 m, then what is the length of the smallest altitude of the triangle? [Give your answer correct to two places of decimal.]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two sides of the triangle = 41 m and 28 m.

Perimeter of the triangle = 84 m.

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a triangle = a + b + c

Area of a triangle using Heron's formula = sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} 

Area of a triangle = (1)/(2) times {base} times {height} 

**Calculation:**

Let the sides of the triangle be a = 41 m, b = 28 m, and c = ?

Perimeter = a + b + c

⇒ 84 = 41 + 28 + c

⇒ c = 84 - 69 = 15 m

Now, semi-perimeter (s) = (a + b + c)/(2)

⇒ s = (84)/(2) = 42 m

Area using Heron's formula:

⇒ Area = sqrt{42(42-41)(42-28)(42-15)} 

⇒ Area = sqrt{42 times 1 times 14 times 27} 

⇒ Area = sqrt{42 times 14 times 27} 

⇒ Area = sqrt{15876} = 126 m²

Now, the smallest altitude corresponds to the longest side (41 m).

Area = (1)/(2) times {base} times {height} 

⇒ 126 = (1)/(2) times 41 times {height} 

⇒ height = (126 times 2)/(41) = (252)/(41)

⇒ height ≈ 6.146 m

**The length of the smallest altitude of the triangle is 6.15 m (correct to two decimal places).**

questions.question: The ratio of currents flowing through two electric circuits is 1 ∶ 4. If the ratio of resistances is 2 ∶ 1. what is the ratio of their powers?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1 ∶ 8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for electric **power** is given by **P = I²R**, where:

 
 
• **P** is the power,
 
• **I** is the current,
 
• **R** is the resistance.
 
 
 
• The ratio of currents in the two circuits is given as **1 ∶ 4**. This means the current in the second circuit is four times that in the first circuit.
 
• The ratio of resistances in the two circuits is given as **2 ∶ 1**. This means the resistance in the first circuit is double that in the second circuit.
 
• To calculate the ratio of powers, substitute the given ratios into the formula for power:
 
 
• For the first circuit: **P₁ = I₁² × R₁**
 
• For the second circuit: **P₂ = I₂² × R₂**
 
 
 
• Now, substitute the given ratios into the expressions for power:
 
 
• **I₁ : I₂ = 1 : 4**, so **I₁² : I₂² = 1² : 4² = 1 : 16**
 
• **R₁ : R₂ = 2 : 1**
 
 
 
• Therefore, the ratio of powers is:
 
 
• **P₁ : P₂ = (I₁² × R₁) : (I₂² × R₂)**
 
• Substitute the values: **P₁ : P₂ = (1 × 2) : (16 × 1) = 2 : 16 = 1 : 8**
 
 
 
• Hence, the ratio of powers in the two circuits is **1 ∶ 8**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important Concept:** The formula for electric power is directly derived from Ohm's law and Joule's law of heating. It forms the basis of many practical applications in electrical engineering.
 
• **Current:** The flow of electric charge is measured in amperes (A). Current plays a critical role in determining the power dissipation in a circuit.
 
• **Resistance:** It opposes the flow of current and is measured in ohms (Ω). Higher resistance in a circuit leads to greater power dissipation.
 
• **Practical Example:** This concept is often used in designing electrical circuits, such as in household appliances, to balance power usage efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles vests the executive powers of the State in the Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 154**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 154 of the Indian Constitution vests the executive powers of the State in the Governor.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state executive and exercises these powers either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
• These executive powers are exercised in accordance with the Indian Constitution and the laws made by the State Legislature.
 
• The Governor's powers include the appointment of the Chief Minister and other ministers, summoning and proroguing the state legislature, and dissolving the legislative assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role and Functions**

 
 
• The Governor acts as a link between the Union Government and the State Government.
 
• They have the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the state extends.
 
• In cases of constitutional crises, the Governor can assume the functions of the government of the state or any of its functions to himself.
 
• The Governor also performs ceremonial duties, such as addressing the state legislature during budget sessions.
 
 
 
• **Executive Powers of the State**
 
 
• The executive power of the state is co-extensive with its legislative power and extends to all matters on which the State Legislature has the power to make laws.
 
• It includes the implementation of laws, maintaining law and order, and ensuring that the provisions of the Constitution are upheld.
 
• These powers are exercised in the name of the Governor, but decisions are taken by the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Governor also has the power to appoint key officials such as the Advocate General and members of the State Public Service Commission.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for the Governor**
 
 
• Article 153: Provides for the appointment of a Governor for each state.
 
• Article 155: The Governor of a state shall be appointed by the President of India.
 
• Article 156: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and for a term of five years.
 
• Article 161: The Governor has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, etc.

questions.question: In an electric motor, the forces acting on the arms of the armature of the motor that are perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field are:

options.text: equal in magnitude and in the same direction
equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
unequal in magnitude and along same direction
unequal in magnitude and in the opposite direction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**equal in magnitude and opposite in direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In an **electric motor**, the armature is a rotating coil placed in a magnetic field.
 
• When an **electric current** passes through the coil, the **magnetic field interacts with the current**, producing forces on the arms of the coil according to the **Fleming's left-hand rule**.
 
• The forces acting on the two opposite arms of the armature are **equal in magnitude** because the current and the magnetic field are the same for both arms.
 
• However, these forces act in **opposite directions** because the current flows in opposite directions in the two arms, resulting in opposite force directions as per the left-hand rule.
 
• This difference in force directions creates a **torque** that rotates the armature, which is the fundamental working principle of an electric motor.
 
• The equal and opposite forces ensure a balanced system, aiding in smooth and efficient rotation of the armature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Equal in magnitude and in the same direction**__

 __
 
• If the forces were in the **same direction**, there would be no rotational motion because the forces would simply move the armature linearly.
 
• This contradicts the principle of torque generation in an electric motor.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Unequal in magnitude and along the same direction**__
 __
 
• Forces of **unequal magnitude** cannot balance the system, leading to instability and improper functioning of the motor.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Unequal in magnitude and in the opposite direction**__
 
 
• If the forces were **unequal**, the armature would experience an unbalanced torque, causing inefficient or erratic rotation.

The image produced by a concave mirror when an object is kept at the centre of the curvature of the mirror is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real and inverted**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed at the center of curvature of a concave mirror, the image formed is **real and inverted**.
 
• The image is formed at the center of curvature itself.
 
• The size of the image is the same as the size of the object.
 
• The focal length of a concave mirror is half of its radius of curvature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror**

 
 
• A concave mirror, also known as a converging mirror, has a reflective surface that curves inward like a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It is used in various applications such as in telescopes, flashlights, and shaving mirrors to focus light.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Mirrors**
 
 
• When the object is placed at the focus of a concave mirror, the image formed is at infinity, real, and inverted.
 
• When the object is placed between the focus and the center of curvature, the image is formed beyond the center of curvature, is real, inverted, and larger than the object.
 
• When the object is placed beyond the center of curvature, the image is formed between the focus and center of curvature, is real, inverted, and smaller than the object.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Equation**
 
 
• The mirror equation is given by 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• This equation helps in determining the nature and position of the image formed by mirrors.

questions.question: Which reaction occurs when a student adds a few drops of lemon in milk?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Precipitation reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When lemon juice is added to milk, it causes the milk to curdle, forming lumps of curd.
 
• This reaction is a classic example of a precipitation reaction.
 
• The citric acid in lemon juice causes the proteins in the milk to denature and coagulate.
 
• The solid particles (curds) formed during this process are the precipitate, and the liquid left behind is whey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction:**

 
 
• A chemical reaction in which a solid is formed in a solution during a chemical reaction.
 
• The solid formed is called the precipitate.
 
• This type of reaction is often used in qualitative chemical analysis.
 
 
 
• **Curdling of Milk:**
 
 
• Occurs when the pH level of milk falls, causing proteins to clump together.
 
• Commonly observed when an acid like lemon juice or vinegar is added to milk.
 
• It is an essential process in the production of cheese and yogurt.
 
 
 
• **Denaturation of Proteins:**
 
 
• A process where proteins lose their structure due to the application of an external stress or compound.
 
• This can be caused by acids, bases, heat, or heavy metals.
 
• Denatured proteins can precipitate out of solution as seen in the curdling of milk.

questions.question: If the cost price of 63 articles is equal to the selling price of 54 articles, then what is the percentage gain or loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If the cost price of 63 articles is equal to the selling price of 54 articles.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Gain = (S - C)/C × 100

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price (CP) of each article be C and Selling Price (SP) of each article be S.

Total CP of 63 articles = 63 × C

Total SP of 54 articles = 54 × S

63 × C = 54 × S

⇒ S/C = 63/54 = 7/6

⇒ S = (7/6)C

Percentage Gain = ((7/6)C - C)/C × 100

⇒ ((7/6)C - C)/C × 100 = (7C - 6C)/(6C) × 100

⇒ C/(6C) × 100

⇒ 1/6 × 100 = 16²/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 16²/₃% gain.**

questions.question: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also termed as the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Morley-Minto Reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
 
• This act was named after John Morley, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Minto, the Viceroy of India.
 
• The act introduced significant changes to the legislative councils in India, including the expansion of the councils and the introduction of separate electorates for Muslims.
 
• The reforms aimed to increase Indian participation in governance while maintaining British control.
 
• These reforms are considered a pivotal moment in the constitutional development of India, marking the beginning of the communal representation in Indian politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Separate Electorates:**

 
 
• The Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims, allowing them to elect their representatives separately.
 
• This system aimed to provide political representation to minority communities but later contributed to communal divisions.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Councils:**
 
 
• The act increased the size of the legislative councils at both the central and provincial levels.
 
• Non-official members were allowed to discuss budgets and ask questions, enhancing their role in governance.
 
 
 
• **John Morley:**
 
 
• John Morley was the Secretary of State for India and played a key role in formulating the 1909 reforms.
 
• He believed in the gradual introduction of self-governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Minto:**
 
 
• Lord Minto was the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910 and collaborated with John Morley on the reforms.
 
• He aimed to balance the demands for Indian participation with the need to maintain British control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Politics:**
 
 
• The introduction of separate electorates had long-term impacts on Indian politics, contributing to communal tensions.
 
• Despite its limitations, the act was a step towards the eventual self-governance of India.

questions.question: The phenomena of scattering of light by colloidal particles gives rise to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tyndall effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light as it passes through a colloid.
 
• This phenomenon is observed when light is scattered by particles in a colloid or in very fine suspensions.
 
• It is named after the 19th-century physicist John Tyndall, who first studied the phenomenon.
 
• The Tyndall effect is responsible for the blue color of the sky and the reddening of the sun at sunset and sunrise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloids**

 
 
• A colloid is a mixture in which one substance consisting of microscopically dispersed insoluble particles is suspended throughout another substance.
 
• Colloids can be solid, liquid, or gas.
 
• Examples of colloids include fog, milk, and butter.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion of Light**
 
 
• Dispersion is the process in which white light separates into its constituent colors when passed through a prism.
 
• This occurs because different colors of light bend by different amounts when they pass through the prism.
 
 
 
• **Refraction of Light**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with a different density.
 
• This is due to the change in speed of light in different media.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection**
 
 
• Total internal reflection occurs when light attempts to move from a denser medium to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing it to be completely reflected within the denser medium.
 
• This principle is used in fiber optics and other applications.

questions.question: If the mean and the mode of a data set are 5 and 8, respectively, then, using the relevant empirical relation, find the median of the same data set.

The Median is always located at exactly 1/3rd of the distance from the Mean towards the Mode.

Total difference (Mode − Mean) = 8 − 5 = 3

Distance from Mean to Median = 1/3 × 3 = 1

Median = Mean + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode for a moderately skewed distribution is:

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

questions.question: There are three pipes A, B and C in a tank. The first pipe A can fill the empty tank in 8 hours, the second pipe B can fill the empty tank in 10 hours, and the third pipe C can empty the completely filled tank in 20 hours. If the three pipes are opened together when the tank is completely empty, then in how many hours will the tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 8 hours.

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 10 hours.

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 20 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Rate of filling or emptying = 1 / Time taken.

**Calculation:**

Rate of filling by pipe A = 1 / 8

Rate of filling by pipe B = 1 / 10

Rate of emptying by pipe C = -1 / 20 (since it is emptying).

Total rate when all three pipes are opened together = (1/8) + (1/10) - (1/20)

Taking LCM of 8, 10, and 20 = 40

Total rate = (5/40) + (4/40) - (2/40) = 7/40

So, the tank will fill at a rate of 7/40 of the tank per hour.

Time taken to fill the tank = 1 / (7/40) = 40 / 7

**The tank will be completely filled in approximately **(40)/(7)** hours.**

• **Tax Revenue:**

• Tax revenue is a major component of revenue receipts.

questions.question: The presence of a magnetic field can be determined by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a magnetic needle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A magnetic needle, or compass, aligns itself with the magnetic field lines, indicating the presence and direction of the magnetic field.
 
• It is a simple and reliable tool to detect the magnetic field, commonly used in navigation and various scientific applications.
 
• When placed in a magnetic field, the needle experiences a torque that aligns it with the field, making it a direct indicator of the magnetic field's direction.
 
• The deflection of the magnetic needle can also provide information about the strength of the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field**

 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• It is generated by electric currents and magnetic dipoles, and it exerts forces on other nearby moving charges and magnetic dipoles.
 
• Magnetic fields can be visualized using magnetic field lines that emanate from the north pole and terminate at the south pole of a magnet.
 
• The unit of magnetic field strength in the International System of Units (SI) is the tesla (T).
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer**
 
 
• A galvanometer is an instrument for detecting and measuring electric current.
 
• It works on the principle that a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a torque.
 
• Although sensitive to magnetic fields, it is not typically used to detect the presence of a magnetic field directly.
 
 
 
• **Ammeter**
 
 
• An ammeter measures the current flowing through a circuit.
 
• It is connected in series with the circuit whose current is to be measured.
 
• While related to magnetic fields, it does not detect magnetic fields directly.
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter**
 
 
• A voltmeter measures the potential difference (voltage) between two points in an electrical circuit.
 
• It is connected in parallel with the component across which the voltage is to be measured.
 
• It is not used to detect magnetic fields.

• **Old Xylem**, also known as heartwood, is the central, non-living part of a tree trunk.
 
• It serves as a storage site for various waste products of the tree.
 
• These waste products include **resins and gums**, which are deposited to avoid their toxic effects on the tree's living tissues.
 
• Resins and gums are complex organic substances that can help protect the tree from pathogens and physical damage.
 
• The accumulation of these substances makes heartwood more resistant to decay and insect attacks compared to the outer, younger wood (sapwood).

• **Resins**: Sticky, organic substances secreted by certain plants, often used in varnishes, adhesives, and incense. They can deter herbivores and protect against pathogens.
 
• **Gums**: Water-soluble polysaccharides produced by plants as a response to injury. They can be used in food, pharmaceuticals, and other industrial applications.
 
• **Xylem**: The vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to the shoots and leaves.

y³ - xy² - x²y + x³

→ y²(y - x) - x²(y - x)

→ (y² - x²)(y - x)

→ (y - x)(y + x)(y - x)

**∴ The correct answer is (y - x)²(y + x).**

questions.question: If ax² - 8x - 8 is divided by (x + 2), then the remainder is 24. Find the value of a.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If ax² - 8x - 8 is divided by (x + 2), then the remainder is 24.

**Formula Used:**

When a polynomial f(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is f(c).

Here, f(x) = ax² - 8x - 8 and c = -2.

Therefore, the remainder is f(-2) = 24.

**Calculation:**

f(-2) = a(-2)² - 8(-2) - 8

⇒ 24 = a(4) + 16 - 8

⇒ 24 = 4a + 8

⇒ 24 - 8 = 4a

⇒ 16 = 4a

⇒ a = 16 / 4

⇒ a = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

questions.question: The sum of the numerator and the denominator of a fraction is 13. If 6 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, then the fraction becomes 8/17. Find the absolute difference between the numerator and the denominator of the given fraction.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of the numerator and the denominator of a fraction is 13.

**Formula Used:**

Let the numerator be x and the denominator be y. Given that x + y = 13. When 6 is added to both numerator and denominator, the fraction becomes (x+6)/(y+6) = 8/17.

**Calculation:**

From the given equations: x + y = 13 and (x+6)/(y+6) = 8/17

⇒ 17(x + 6) = 8(y + 6)

⇒ 17x + 102 = 8y + 48

⇒ 17x - 8y = -54

We now have two equations:

1) x + y = 13

2) 17x - 8y = -54

Solving these equations:

From equation 1: y = 13 - x

Substitute y in equation 2:

⇒ 17x - 8(13 - x) = -54

⇒ 17x - 104 + 8x = -54

⇒ 25x - 104 = -54

⇒ 25x = 50

⇒ x = 2

Substitute x back into equation 1:

⇒ 2 + y = 13

⇒ y = 11

The absolute difference between the numerator and the denominator is:

⇒ |x - y| = |2 - 11| = 9

**The correct answer is 9.**

questions.question: The simple interest for 6 years, at a certain rate of interest per annum, is one-sixth of the principal. At the same rate of simple interest, what sum of money will amount to Rs. 6,000 total in 3 years? [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple interest for 6 years is one-sixth of the principal.

We are required to find the sum of money that will amount to Rs. 6,000 in 3 years at the same rate of interest per annum.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Where:

P = Principal

R = Rate of interest per annum

T = Time in years

**Calculation:**

Let the principal be P and the rate of interest be R per annum.

The simple interest for 6 years is given as (P × R × 6) / 100.

We are also given that the simple interest for 6 years is one-sixth of the principal:

(P × R × 6) / 100 = P / 6

⇒ P × R × 6 = P × 100 / 6

⇒ R = 100 / 36

⇒ R = 2.78% per annum.

Now, using this rate of interest, we are required to find the principal that will amount to Rs. 6,000 in 3 years.

Let the principal be X. The amount after 3 years will be given by:

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Amount = X + (X × 2.78 × 3) / 100

Amount = X + (8.34X) / 100

Amount = X × (1 + 8.34 / 100)

Amount = X × 1.0834

We are told that the amount is Rs. 6,000, so:

X × 1.0834 = 6,000

⇒ X = 6,000 / 1.0834

⇒ X ≈ 5,538.46

**The required sum of money is approximately Rs. 5,538.46.**

questions.question: If the product of the ages of M and N is 486 years and the ratio of their ages is 3 ∶ 2, what is the sum of their ages?

questions.question: For a given concave mirror of focal length 0.5 m if the object distance is 0.6 m, then the magnification produced is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnification (m) in a concave mirror is given by the formula **m = -v/u**, where 'v' is the image distance and 'u' is the object distance.
 
• Using the mirror formula, **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where 'f' is the focal length, we can determine the image distance 'v'.
 
• Given: Focal length (f) = -0.5 m (since it is a concave mirror), Object distance (u) = -0.6 m.
 
• Substituting the given values into the mirror formula: **1/-0.5 = 1/v + 1/-0.6**.
 
• Solving for 'v', we get: **v = - 3 m**. Thus, the magnification (m) = -(-3)/(-0.6) = - 5.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror, or converging mirror, has a reflecting surface that is recessed inward (away from the incident light).
 
• Such mirrors are used in applications where converging light is required, such as in reflecting telescopes and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula relates object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) as: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• This formula is applicable for both concave and convex mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• Magnification (m) is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object.
 
• In mirrors, it is also given by the formula: **m = -v/u**.
 
• If magnification is negative, the image is inverted relative to the object.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• In the mirror formula, distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive, while those measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
 
• For concave mirrors, focal length (f) is negative.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution says that no child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous jobs.
 
• This provision aims to protect children from exploitation and hazardous working conditions.
 
• Article 24 is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution, specifically under the Right against Exploitation.
 
• The enforcement of Article 24 is crucial for ensuring child welfare and safeguarding their rights to education and healthy development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986:**

 
 
• This Act prohibits the employment of children in certain hazardous occupations and processes.
 
• It also regulates the conditions of work for children in non-hazardous occupations and processes.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009:**
 
 
• This Act ensures free and compulsory education for all children aged 6 to 14 years in India.
 
• It aims to eliminate child labour by ensuring that children are in schools rather than workplaces.
 
 
 
• **National Child Labour Project (NCLP) Scheme:**
 
 
• Implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, this scheme focuses on rehabilitating children withdrawn from work.
 
• It provides education and vocational training to rescued child labourers.
 
 
 
• **International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions:**
 
 
• India has ratified ILO Conventions No. 138 (minimum age for employment) and No. 182 (worst forms of child labour).
 
• These conventions aim to combat child labour and ensure children's rights worldwide.

questions.question: The correct relation between refractive index (μ), speed of light in air (c) and speed of light in the medium (v) is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**μ = (c) / (v)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The refractive index (μ) of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (c) to the speed of light in the medium (v).
 
• The formula is given by μ = c / v, where c is the speed of light in vacuum (approximately 3 x 10⁸ m/s) and v is the speed of light in the medium.
 
• The refractive index indicates how much the light slows down when it enters the medium from a vacuum.
 
• A higher refractive index means that light travels slower in the medium compared to a vacuum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Light in Vacuum (c):**

 
 
• The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second (m/s).
 
• This is considered a fundamental constant in physics.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index (μ):**
 
 
• The refractive index is a dimensionless number that describes how light propagates through a medium.
 
• It is denoted by the Greek letter μ (mu).
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Snell's Law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of two media.
 
• The law is given by n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂, where n is the refractive index and θ is the angle.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refractive Index:**
 
 
• Refractive index is used in designing lenses and optical instruments.
 
• It is crucial in determining the focusing power of lenses.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion:**
 
 
• Dispersion occurs when light separates into its constituent colors due to varying refractive indices for different wavelengths.
 
• This phenomenon is observed in prisms and rainbows.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were added by which amendment to the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This amendment inserted a new part, **Part IVA**, which is titled "Fundamental Duties."
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties; an eleventh duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act**

 
 
• Passed during the Emergency period, the 42nd Amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it made.
 
• It aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the strength of the executive and legislature.
 
• Besides adding Fundamental Duties, it also laid down the Directive Principles of State Policy as fundamental to the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A**
 
 
• Article 51A outlines the Fundamental Duties of the citizens of India.
 
• These duties include respect for the Constitution, the national flag, the national anthem, and more.
 
• One of the duties added was to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act**
 
 
• Enacted in 2002, this amendment made education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It also added the 11th Fundamental Duty, which requires parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children.
 
 
 
• **Non-justiciable Nature**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, meaning no legal action can be taken for their violation.
 
• They serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a sense of discipline and commitment.

questions.question: The age of Raghu 8 years ago was thrice the then age of Mohan. Eight years hence, Raghu's age will be twice of Mohan's age. Find the ratio of the present ages of Mohan and Raghu, respectively.
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the present ages of Raghu and Mohan be R and M, respectively.

Eight years ago:

R - 8 = 3 × (M - 8)

Eight years hence:

R + 8 = 2 × (M + 8)

From the first equation:

R - 8 = 3M - 24

⇒ R = 3M - 16

From the second equation:

R + 8 = 2M + 16

⇒ R = 2M + 8

Now, equating both expressions for R:

3M - 16 = 2M + 8

⇒ 3M - 2M = 8 + 16

⇒ M = 24

Substituting **M = 24** in **R = 2M + 8**:

R = 2(24) + 8 = 48 + 8 = 56

**Ratio of present ages of Mohan to Raghu:**

M : R = 24 : 56

Reducing the ratio:

= 3 : 7

**∴ The ratio of Mohan’s age to Raghu’s age is 3 : 7.**

**Given:**

Let the two numbers be a and b.

LCM = 10 × HCF

LCM + HCF = 451

a + b = 287

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = a × b

**Calculation:**

From the given equation:

HCF + 10 × HCF = 451

⇒ 11 × HCF = 451

⇒ HCF = 451 / 11 = 41

LCM = 10 × 41 = 410

LCM × HCF = a × b

⇒ 410 × 41 = a × b

⇒ a × b = 16810

Now, we solve for a and b:

a + b = 287

a × b = 16810

Solving the quadratic equation:

t² - 287t + 16810 = 0

Using the quadratic formula: t = [-(-287) ± √(287² - 4 × 16810)] / 2

= [287 ± √(82369 - 67240)] / 2

= [287 ± √15129] / 2

= [287 ± 123] / 2

Possible values:

a = (287 + 123) / 2 = 410 / 2 = 205

b = (287 - 123) / 2 = 164 / 2 = 82

**∴ One of the numbers is 82.**

questions.question: What is the position of zinc in the Modern Periodic Table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 12, Period 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zinc (Zn) is located in Group 12 of the Modern Periodic Table, which is part of the d-block elements.
 
• It is positioned in Period 4, indicating that it has four electron shells.
 
• Zinc has the atomic number 30, which means it has 30 protons in its nucleus.
 
• The electron configuration of zinc is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transition Metals:**

 
 
• Zinc is classified as a transition metal, which typically have partially filled d orbitals.
 
• Transition metals are known for their ability to form colored compounds and their use as catalysts in various chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Group 12 Elements:**
 
 
• Group 12 includes zinc (Zn), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg).
 
• These elements are characterized by having a filled d¹⁰ subshell in their most stable oxidation states.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Zinc:**
 
 
• Zinc is widely used for galvanizing iron to protect it from corrosion.
 
• It is also an essential trace element necessary for the proper function of numerous enzymes in the human body.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Trends:**
 
 
• As you move across a period in the periodic table, the atomic number increases, and the elements show a gradual change in properties.
 
• Down a group, the atomic size increases, and the elements tend to become more metallic in nature.
